title: Day and Night 4
content:
A beat of silence.

"Let go," Wei Wuxian pleaded.

Lan Wangji sat tall and proud, keeping an icy, deadpan stare fixed on him. Leaning in slightly, he slid his teeth from the first knuckle down to the second—and bit down even harder.

"Ow, ow, hurts!"

Only then did Lan Wangji ease his jaw. Wei Wuxian scrambled backward, dragging his throbbing finger out of the dragon’s den. The bite gave him full-body goosebumps; anything that clamped its jaws on him instantly triggered his deeply ingrained canine trauma, sending his hackles straight up.

Before he could put some actual distance between them, Lan Wangji unsheathed Bichen with a violent snap, driving the blade down into the floor mat and pinning the hem of Wei Wuxian’s robes to the timber.

The clothes they wore had been provided back at Lotus Pier—woven from high-grade spiritual fabric that resisted tearing. Anchored to the floorboards by his pinned hem, Wei Wuxian couldn't roll away. Flustered, he babbled, "Lan Zhan, look at what you did! You just punched a hole straight through their mat and into the floor! You're gonna have to pay for that..."

Before the sentence cleared his mouth, an iron hand snatched him by the collar and yanked him backward. Wei Wuxian’s spine slammed flush against a solid chest, and Lan Wangji’s low, rumbling voice grated right in his ear:

"Will pay."

With that, Lan Wangji ripped Bichen out of the floorboards, raising the sword as if planning to carve a few more holes for good measure. Wei Wuxian threw himself across the blade in a panic. "Hold it! Stop right there! What's gotten into you? A couple of drops of wine and you turn into a regular menace?!"

His tone carried clear scolding. Lan Wangji blinked. He glanced down at Wei Wuxian, stared at his own hand, and then looked at the mangled floorboards. As if suddenly waking up to his crime, he tossed the sword away.

Bichen clattered against the floorboards with a dull thud, rolling across the room. Wei Wuxian gripped the scabbard, hooked a toe under the rolling hilt, and flicked his foot upward. With effortless precision, Bichen slid cleanly home into its sheath.

Wei Wuxian wagged a finger. "Don't go throwing dangerous weapons around."

Hearing the reprimand, Lan Wangji tucked his chin and sat up even straighter, the very picture of a contrite, model student taking his discipline to heart. It was always Lan Wangji giving the stern, righteous lectures; only when the Second Young Master of Lan was plastered out of his mind did Wei Wuxian ever get the upper hand.

Folding his arms over his chest with Bichen cradled in the crook of his elbow, Wei Wuxian tilted his head, shaking with suppressed laughter.

Gods, he loved drunken Lan Wangji.

The moment Lan Wangji was tipsy, the suffocating awkwardness and walking-on-eggshells anxiety that had weighed Wei Wuxian down for days vanished into thin air. All the pent-up teasing he hadn't dared unleash suddenly found its playground.

Pacing around the rigidly poised cultivator, Wei Wuxian circled back, sliding down onto the mat right beside him. He pinched the punctured hem of his robe, waving the torn fabric under Lan Wangji's nose. "Look at the mess you made. You tore my clothes. You’re patching this up for me later, you hear me?"

Lan Wangji nodded solemnly.

"Do you even know how to sew?"

Lan Wangji gave a slight shake of his head.

"Knew it," Wei Wuxian snorted. "Well, you'd better learn, because you're the one fixing it. Understood?"

Watching Lan Wangji nod in earnest agreement again, Wei Wuxian picked up a floor cushion, utterly satisfied. Before anyone could see the evidence, he tossed the cushion directly over the puncture wound in the floorboards. "There. I hid the hole for you. Now nobody will catch you playing vandal."

Lan Wangji reached inside his lapel, pulled out his delicate, embroidered money pouch, and shoved it in front of Wei Wuxian's nose, shaking it vigorously. "Pay."

Wei Wuxian chuckled, "I know you're loaded. Put it away, put it—hey, what are you doing?"

Lan Wangji stuffed the pouch straight into Wei Wuxian’s robes.

Feeling the heavy bulge resting against his ribs, Wei Wuxian blinked. "For me?"

Having shoved the coin purse inside, Lan Wangji carefully smoothed down Wei Wuxian’s collar, patting his chest with deliberate, firm taps as if making sure it wouldn't slip out. "Keep it safe."

"You're actually giving this to me? All of it?"

"Mm."

Broke-as-dirt Wei Wuxian beamed with theatrical gratitude. "Much obliged! I'm rich!"

The moment the words left his mouth, Lan Wangji’s brows knit tight. Without warning, his hand plunged back into Wei Wuxian’s robes, snatching the purse right back.

"No!"

Watching his newly acquired fortune slip through his fingers, Wei Wuxian gaped. "No what?"

Lan Wangji wore a deeply disappointed, tightly reined-in scowl. He tucked the money pouch away with a sullen, spiritless shake of his head, looking genuinely heartbroken.

Wei Wuxian leaned in, confused. "Didn't you just say it was mine? Why take it back? Backtracking on your word now?"

Lan Wangji turned his entire body away. Wei Wuxian caught him by the shoulders, steering him back around to coax him: "Look at me. Don't run off. Come on, look at me."

So Lan Wangji looked.

The two locked eyes, inches apart. They were close enough that Wei Wuxian could have counted every single one of Lan Wangji’s long, sweeping lashes. The cool, clean fragrance of sandalwood mingled with the heady, sweet warmth of liquor, weaving together between every shallow breath.

Staring into those pale eyes, Wei Wuxian felt his pulse hammering faster and faster. His courage failed him, and he broke the stare, awkwardly averting his gaze.

"Fine!" he conceded quickly. "You win. Let's play something else. Same rules as before: I ask, you answer, and no ly—"

The moment the word 'play' left his mouth, Lan Wangji lit up. "Okay!"

He seized Wei Wuxian’s wrist, shot across the room like a gust of wind, and dragged him down the stairs. Wei Wuxian stumbled through the ground-floor lobby in a daze. The landlady and her staff were gathered around a long table eating dinner; Lan Wangji didn't spare them a single glance, plowing straight for the exit with Wei Wuxian in tow.

The landlady pushed back her stool, calling out, "What's the rush, young masters? Was the food not to your liking?"

Wei Wuxian managed to yell over his shoulder, "It was great! Especially the wine—real kick to it—!"

Before he could finish, Lan Wangji had yanked him out the front door and onto the street.

Even out on the open thoroughfare, Lan Wangji showed zero sign of slowing down, sprinting like his robes were on fire. Panting, Wei Wuxian yelled, "Where on earth are you taking me?!"

Lan Wangji didn't utter a peep. He tore down the street, skidding to an abrupt halt in front of a private residential courtyard.

Wei Wuxian opened his mouth to ask what the game was, but Lan Wangji raised an index finger to his lips. "Shh."

Slipping an arm around Wei Wuxian’s waist, Lan Wangji lightly kicked off the flagstones, lifting them both onto the tiled roof of the perimeter wall. Perched over the eaves, Lan Wangji whispered, "Look."

Intrigued by the sheer secrecy of it all, Wei Wuxian followed his laser-focused gaze down into the yard—landing squarely on a chicken coop.

Wei Wuxian deadpanned, "You dragged me all the way out here to look at a chicken coop?"

Lan Wangji murmured, "Let's go."

"Go do what?"

Lan Wangji had already vaulted off the wall, dropping silently into the center of the courtyard.

If the owner had been awake to witness an ethereal, white-robed immortal descending bathed in moonlight, they would have dropped to their knees, weeping at the arrival of a heavenly deity. But Lan Wangji’s current behavior lacked any shred of immortal grace. He tiptoed across the yard like a common thief, feeling his way in the dark.

Sensing trouble, Wei Wuxian dropped down after him, tugging on the tail of his forehead ribbon. "What are you actually doing?"

Lan Wangji pressed a hand over his forehead ribbon with one hand, plunging his free arm straight into the coop.

The sleeping hens woke in a shrieking panic, flapping their wings and scrambling in all directions. Lan Wangji’s eyes sharpened. His hand struck like lightning, snatching the plumpest, fattest bird in the coop right by its plumage.

Wei Wuxian stood completely dumbfounded.

The speckled hen squawked and flailed in Lan Wangji’s iron grip. With absolute solemnity, Lan Wangji turned and shoved the bird straight into Wei Wuxian’s arms.

"What is this?" Wei Wuxian blurted out.

Lan Wangji answered flatly, "A chicken."

"I can see it's a chicken! Why are you giving me a chicken?!"

Lan Wangji’s jaw set into an unyielding line. "A gift for you."

"A gift... alright, fine." Figuring the man would throw another tantrum if he turned it down, Wei Wuxian awkwardly cradled the flailing hen against his ribs. "Lan Zhan, do you even realize what you're doing? This chicken belongs to someone. This is called stealing."

The peerless, renowned Hanguang-jun... If word got out that he got sloshed and went around poaching backyard poultry in the dead of night, the cultivation world’s collective jaw would shatter.

Dracing the line, drunk Lan Wangji only heard what he felt like hearing. Tuning out the lecture entirely, he dived back into the coop. Inside, clucks, squawks, and flapping feathers erupted into a chaotic, tragic symphony.

Wei Wuxian muttered to the night air, "For the record: I didn't tell him to do this."

Before long, both of them were vaulting back over the wall, each cradling a trembling, ruffled hen. Pacing down the alley, Wei Wuxian was still scratching his head over why Lan Wangji had suddenly turned into a poultry thief—was he hungry?—when he caught sight of a stray white feather clinging to Lan Wangji’s immaculate black hair.

Wei Wuxian snorted, unable to take it anymore. He reached out to pluck the feather away, but Lan Wangji leaped into the air again, perching neatly on a high branch overhead.

The tree grew inside someone’s private garden, but its sprawling boughs hung heavy over the outer wall. Sitting astride a branch, Lan Wangji looked down.

Wei Wuxian craned his neck. "What now?!"

Lan Wangji leaned over the edge. "Shh."

Hearing that hush, Wei Wuxian braced himself for another petty crime. Sure enough, Lan Wangji reached out, snapped something from the canopy, and lobbed it downward. Cradling the hen with one arm, Wei Wuxian caught the projectile with his free hand.

Opening his palm, he found a plump, round jujube, mottled in green and crimson.

Of course. First the chickens, now the fruit!

Poaching chickens and stripping fruit trees were practically second nature to Wei Wuxian; in his youth, he had loved nothing more than leading a rowdy pack of disciples on midnight orchard raids. But replacing his delinquent teenage buddies with Lan Wangji was downright surreal. Actually, strike that—Lan Wangji wasn't an accomplice here; he was the mastermind running the whole operation.

Right then, a spark went off in Wei Wuxian’s head.

Earlier at Lotus Pier, while walking Lan Wangji through the grounds of his youth, he had rattled off a laundry list of his childhood antics—including quite a few "glorious achievements" just like this.

Did he actually take all those stories to heart? Did he want to experience it for himself?

It made too much sense!

The Gusu Lan Clan's discipline was suffocatingly strict. Lan Wangji had spent his entire childhood locked inside copying scriptures and studying calligraphy, measuring every breath and step against the unyielding standards of his elders. He’d never had the chance to run wild and raise hell. Since he couldn't do it sober, was he using drunkenness as an excuse to finally live a little?

Up in the branches, Lan Wangji’s hands moved like a whirlwind. Within moments, he had picked the entire tree bone-dry, stripping every single jujube from its twigs. Stuffing them all into his Qiankun pouch, he finally dropped down from the wall, opening the fabric to proudly display his hard-earned spoils.

Staring down at the mountain of plump fruit, Wei Wuxian was momentarily at a loss for words.

After a long pause, he gave an enthusiastic thumbs-up. "...They're huge. So many of them! Truly impressive! Beautifully done!"
